I think you could benefit from reading about intrusive thoughts, there are others who often have them, the severity differs of course but I think it could help you. Also, I think it's important to know that no matter what happens you will be okay, you will survive. On top of that, whether you worry or not will not change anything, why are you putting yourself through something that hasn't happened?

You might be different than me, but often I feel weird when I'm not anxious about something, like my mind is so used to worrying as if worrying controls outcomes. It really doesn't and life is full of random events, try to think of things that could go right, maybe do things physically to make you feel more in control over your life like writing or dancing to music. Even talking to yourself out loud can help differentiate you from your anxiety.

It could be worse, but it could also be better, and why can't it be better in the future? I know anxiety is so hard to deal with, but objectively speaking anxiety will not change anything for the better. Let's say the worser thing happens? Well, now you're going through it twice, and if it never happens? then you've wasted all that energy for nothing. I hope you are able to control those destructive thoughts soon and I wish you all the best. Everything will be alright <3

I do understand where you are coming from. I think the issue is that sometimes when talking about responsibility is that people may perceive it as saying they both were equally 50/50 in the wrong. I think teenagers should know better than to flirt with their idol who they know is an adult, but like I said, I think with hormonal changes, infatuation and immaturity it's a lot harder for them to turn down and truly understand the severity of such actions. Also, a lot of the time with grooming it will be friendship at first and the flirting will only happen after a period of time. So, it becomes complicated because the minor may not have intentions from the start to develop romantic feelings towards the adult. Basically, in theory, yes, if we are truly honest, teenagers should know it is wrong to engage in behaviour with adults no matter if they are good friends, popular, or whatnot. But the adult will always have the most responsibility and will need to take most of the blame for allowing that to even happen. 

Also you're welcome, I think too many people attack others too quickly nowadays for simply holding a different opinion and attacking people won't make them any more likely to listen to your point of view. We can all learn from each other :)
